summary: Tested Forgot Password (WhatsApp OTP) feature end-to-end. Backend: 7/7 pytest cases pass (unknown email 200 no-enum, valid email → masked hint + SHA-256 hashed OTP, 45s cooldown, 3 wrong attempts invalidate OTP, correct OTP mints reset_token, single-use reset_token rejects reuse, new-password login works while old fails). Frontend: full 3-step wizard works — /login Forgot? link → /forgot-password step 1 (email) → step 2 (6 OTP boxes with paste + 45s resend countdown) → step 3 (new+confirm password with eye toggle) → redirect to /login → sign in with new password → /employee with 'Welcome back, Maya' toast.

integration_issues.issue: verify-otp is invoked twice per completion (one successful, one immediate 400). Root cause: setTimeout(onComplete) is scheduled from inside the setState updater function, so React 18 StrictMode double-invokes it in dev. Harmless in prod, but in dev it consumes an attempt against the freshly-verified (now used=true) OTP → visible 400 in devtools right after the success. Fix: schedule onComplete outside the updater (e.g., via a useEffect that watches otp completeness) or guard onComplete with a ref.

Backend returns 200 with {throttled:true} and no new OTP is created; frontend still advances to step 2 and shows 'We sent a code on WhatsApp to …9999', misleading the user. Consider surfacing a distinct message when data.throttled === true (e.g., 'You've requested too many codes. Please try again in an hour.') and/or NOT clearing the previous OTP boxes.

action_items: (Nice-to-have) Move onComplete scheduling out of the setState updater to avoid StrictMode double-fire and the resulting stray verify-otp 400.
(Nice-to-have) Handle {throttled:true} response distinctly on the frontend so throttled users see a meaningful message instead of being sent to the OTP screen.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py forgot_password: throttled branch returns {throttled:true} but does NOT create a new OTP; frontend cannot distinguish. Consider adding a distinct message field the UI can display, or returning cooldown-style behaviour (empty phone_hint or explicit user-facing detail).
OTP is hashed with SHA-256 (good, matches spec) and compared via hmac.compare_digest (constant-time). ✓
reset-password correctly binds JTI on OTP so token reuse is blocked and returns 'This reset link has already been used' on the second call. ✓

Frontend OtpBoxes.set() schedules setTimeout(onComplete) inside the setState updater — React 18 StrictMode dev-mode side effect causes onComplete to be called twice. Recommend moving auto-verify trigger to a useEffect that watches otp completeness.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing maya@acme.com. Temporarily disabled db.whatsapp_configs.enabled during tests, re-enabled after. Restored maya password to Demo@123 after tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: OTP is exposed in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log ONLY when tenant's whatsapp_configs.enabled=false. Rate limits: 45s cooldown, 5 sends/hour (rolling). To avoid throttling between test runs, delete db.password_reset_otps for the test email. Password reset regenerates the login lockout row so a subsequent Demo@123 login will get 401 (not lockout).
